Skala Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Skała, Poland

Demolished. Skała's main Jewish cemetery, likely established around the turn of the 20th century (certainly before 1924), was originally wood-fenced before an 1920s stone wall replacement added a gated entrance and funeral house. Jews first settled in Skała at the end of the 18th century, initially under Olkusz's kehilla, with an independent community from 1924; population reached 731 by 1937. An open ghetto formed in spring 1941 held 1,500-3,000 Jews, with some deported via Słomniki to Bełżec in August 1942 and others murdered directly in town or at this cemetery, which also served as an execution site during the war. In 1943, Germans ordered the wall demolished, using its material to pave Powstańców Street. Poland fenced the site again in 1988, adding a Holocaust memorial; further renovation followed in 2008, though an information board installed then was found overturned by 2020.
